note: Pinned build inputs: pixi, Mojo, and ninja are exact; system clang, bpftool, cmake, and dev-only Python carry minimum floors (default install per environment). Verify with: pixi install && tools/build --check-toolchain. The pixi.lock file carries authoritative conda package hashes; this file records the selected versions and their provenance.

libbpf_source.note: Consumed through the libbpf-mojo bridge; MemVeil never links libbpf directly.

clang.note: Floor; verified with Ubuntu 26.04 clang 21.1.8 and Fedora 44 clang 22.1.8.

bpftool.note: Floor; verified with Ubuntu 26.04 bpftool 7.7.0 and Fedora 44 bpftool 7.6.0.

cmake.role: native build driver; default install in each environment

python.role: development validation only; never runtime collection or replay

product_contracts.note: External record contracts live in schemas/; event, profile, doctor, report and receipt schemas are versioned independently; native bridge ABI is owned by libbpf-mojo. Each family ships its current contract plus any retained (superseded but still shipped) contracts pinned here.

libbpf-mojo.note: Clean, untagged 0.2.3 development candidate from the exact committed source above; not a published v0.2.3 release or a live-qualified artifact. ABI 1 and SONAME are unchanged. Consumed by path (LMB_PACKAGE) plus this exact hash or the vendored tarball. Corresponding first-party and pinned libbpf source, notices and provenance are included under third_party/. Ordinary live and compiler-free clean-room gates remain pending; confidential-platform qualification is separate.

platform_floor.kernel: attempt-trace >= 6.0; mapping-lifecycle and copy-actual >= 6.11; BTF required; qualification ceiling 7.3 (not a refusal ceiling); doctor, help, version, and offline report have no kernel floor
platform_floor.note: A version string is eligibility only. Each capability needs its own profile and live evidence.

decisions: D1: pixi (pixi.toml + pixi.lock) is the Mojo project manifest; one manifest per repository.
D2: Mojo 1.2.0 stable from the public max channel; nightly builds are not used.
D3: libbpf is consumed only through the pinned libbpf-mojo bridge, never linked directly.

D4: System clang carries a minimum floor (21.1.8) for C eBPF compilation: vendors ship different builds of nearby versions, so an exact string would single-distro the build. Bit-reproducibility is claimed only for CI-built artifacts; a local build is not the CI binary. Revisit on BPF codegen issues.
D5: Validation tooling uses Python standard library only; no third-party Python dependencies.
D6: External schema version 0.1.0 is independent of product, bridge ABI, and BPF wire versions.

D7: cmake is a build driver, not a codegen input: the check enforces a minimum version (default install per environment), not an exact pin. System clang, bpftool, and dev-only Python carry floors for the same multi-distro reason; pixi, Mojo, and ninja stay exact.
